## Status: proposal only
No scenarios have been built or run. This page lays out a methodology sketch,
how it would map onto this framework, and the decisions needed before any
model time is spent. Nothing below reflects real model output.
:::

## The question

> Maybe a combination approach could be useful? What if we calculated and
> compared the additional Congested Roadway Capacity Demand (physical space
> e.g. lane-mile minutes) from an extra 500 or 1000 typical households added
> to specific locations around the region? We would use the TDM to estimate
> the amount of peak-period roadway capacity added (which would include the
> space-time footprint of the new households and their impact on delay for
> others), based on the roadway travel that they would add to the system
> (allowing for different modes to be chosen, and travel across the day for
> various activities).
>
> This would be a measure of the burden placed on the system to access their
> daily needs and opportunities, and it could be expressed as a percentage of
> the burden placed by adding the extra HH to the geographic center of the
> region which is in Murray. *"A household placed in Western Davis County
> puts 1.6x more burden on the system"* — but if it's in one of Davis
> County's identified City and Town Centers, it's only 1.2x as much burden.

## Proposed methodology

**Design:** one converged **Base** run, one **Control** run (Base + N
households added at a Murray TAZ — the geographic-center reference), and one
**Test** run per candidate site (Base + the same N households added at that
site's TAZ). Same household count everywhere, so differences reflect
*location*, not household mix.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    SE[Base SE data] --> Base[Base run<br/>no HH added]
    SE -->|+N HH at Murray| Control[Control run]
    SE -->|+N HH at Site A| SiteA[Test: Site A]
    SE -->|+N HH at Site B| SiteB[Test: Site B]
    SE -->|+N HH at Site …| SiteN[Test: Site …]

    Base --> Metric[ΔVHT = Test − Base<br/>peak periods, congested V/C tiers]
    Control --> Metric
    SiteA --> Metric
    SiteB --> Metric
    SiteN --> Metric

    Metric --> Index["Burden Index(site) =<br/>ΔVHT(site) / ΔVHT(Murray control)"]
```

**Metric:** systemwide congested vehicle-hours-traveled (ΔVHT), not just the
new households' own trips — the whole point is capturing the delay imposed
on *everyone else*, which only shows up as a regionwide before/after
difference. Peak periods (AM, PM), filtered to links at or above a
congestion threshold (V/C ≥ 0.8 and/or ≥ 1.0).

**Burden Index** = ΔVHT(site) ÷ ΔVHT(Murray control) — giving the
"1.6x" / "1.2x" style figure directly.

## Baseline signal, from the existing 2023 run

Real numbers, not simulated — computed directly from the segment-level
network summary already curated for the `v10.0-beta.2-2023` base run
(`runs/v10.0-beta.2/v10.0-beta.2-2023/outputs/_Summary_SEGID_filtered.csv`),
which is a converged 2023 highway assignment already sitting in this repo.
No new Cube Voyager run was needed to produce this table — it's a direct
aggregation of that file's per-segment volume/capacity/VHT fields, the same
V/C≥0.8 / V/C≥1.0 tiering `02_Summarize_HighwayNet.s` would apply, just done
in Python against data that already exists.

| Period | Total VHT | VHT at V/C ≥ 0.8 | VHT at V/C ≥ 1.0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| AM | 225,355 | 66,522 (29.5%) | 17,225 (7.6%) |
| MD | 405,888 | 43,243 (10.7%) | 908 (0.2%) |
| PM | 338,003 | 146,780 (43.4%) | 51,135 (15.1%) |
| EV | 312,990 | 115 (0.0%) | 0 (0.0%) |

Regionwide lane-miles in this network: **9,014** (segment-direction rows).

This is *system scale*, not the site-comparison metric itself — it's today's
regionwide congested-VHT backdrop that a 500–1000-household ΔVHT would be
measured against. PM is the most congested period by a wide margin (43% of
all PM vehicle-hours occur on links at V/C≥0.8); AM is a distant second; MD
and EV carry almost no V/C≥1.0 congestion. This confirms AM+PM is the right
peak-period scope for the Burden Index, and suggests PM alone may show the
clearest site-to-site differences.

::: {.callout-note}
## Reusing this run as the study's Base scenario
This converged run is the natural `base` scenario for the actual study (see
"How this fits the run-management framework" below) — its raw scenario
folder can be seeded via `start_from_copy` and resumed at post-processing
once the BCA-summary driver-script edit is in place, rather than re-running
full feedback from scratch. It hasn't been registered under the
`household-location-burden` run set yet; that's a quick step once the site
list is ready.
:::

## What the model already gives us to work with

This isn't hypothetical — the pieces exist in the TDM today, just not wired
together for this purpose:

| Need | Existing TDM piece | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Systemwide VMT/VHT by period, purpose, and congestion tier (V/C ≥ 0.8, ≥ 1.0) | `2_ModelScripts/7_PostProcessing/4_BCA_Summaries/02_Summarize_HighwayNet.s` | Exists, does exactly this — but its `READ FILE` line is **commented out** in the default driver script, so it doesn't currently run |
| A way to add households to a specific TAZ without touching anything else | `WFRC_SEFile` / `MAG_SEFile` — plain TAZ-level `TOTHH`/`HHPOP` CSVs | Exists; this framework already has a proven pattern for generating per-scenario SE variants (used for the `non-motorized-2023` study) |
| A converged 2023 base network to build on | The `v10.0-beta.2` run set's `Base_2023` scenario, already run in this repo | Exists and converged — reusable as the Base run rather than starting from scratch |
| Household composition (size, income, workers, autos) for the "typical household" | `1_HHDisag_AutoOwn/` (LifeCycle → HHDisaggregation → AutoOwnership) | The model derives this itself from `TOTHH`/`HHPOP`, using distributions that already respond to local accessibility — there's no separate lever to force a specific household profile |
| Tighter convergence / warm-start across runs, to keep a 500–1000 HH signal from being swamped by run-to-run noise | — | **Not found.** No iteration-count, RMSE, or warm-start key is exposed in the Control Center. This needs an answer from whoever maintains the TDM's feedback-loop scripts before results can be trusted at this small a scale |

## How this fits the run-management framework

Mechanically, this would be a new run set — `household-location-burden` —
following the same pattern already proven by `non-motorized-2023` and
`bring-work-trips-closer-to-home`:

- **`base`** scenario — reuse the existing converged `v10.0-beta.2-2023`
  run rather than re-running full feedback from scratch (seed its folder via
  `start_from_copy`, then resume just the post-processing steps with
  `start_at_label` to pick up the newly-enabled BCA summary output).
- **`control-murray`** and one **`site-<name>`** scenario per candidate
  location — each pointed at its own generated SE file via
  `overrides.WFRC_SEFile`, the same relative-path mechanism
  `non-motorized-2023` uses.
- A shared **custom driver script** (this run set's own copy of
  `__HailMary_1Subfolder.s`, with the BCA summary line turned on) — the
  framework's existing `driver_script` mechanism, no core code changes
  needed.
- **Outputs curated**: just the small `Summary_HighwayNet.csv` per
  scenario — well under the size ceiling, no raw network/matrix files
  committed.
- A small Burden Index calculation module, reported here once real runs
  exist — same shape as `non-motorized-2023`'s `report_loader.py`.

No changes to the TDM codebase, the orchestrator's core logic, or how Cube
Voyager runs are required — this is entirely new configuration plus one
custom driver script, the same category of work as every other run set in
this repo.

## Decisions needed before building this

| Decision | Options | Recommendation | If left unresolved |
|---|---|---|---|
| **N** — households per site | 500 or 1000 | 1000, for a stronger signal against regional noise (see convergence risk below) | Defaults to 500 (boss's first-mentioned number) |
| **Congestion threshold** | V/C ≥ 0.8, ≥ 1.0, or report both | Report both — cheap, since both are already in the same summary CSV | Defaults to reporting both |
| **Peak window** | AM+PM only, or all four periods | AM+PM, matching "peak-period" in the original ask; MD/EV available in the same file if wanted later | Defaults to AM+PM |
| **Site list** | Western Davis County, Davis County's designated City/Town Centers (Wasatch Choice RCP centers), plus other target geographies | Needs a real TAZ list. No City/Town Centers layer was found in this repo's TDM inputs — likely needs to come from WFRC's regional centers GIS layer | **Blocks starting the build** — this is the one open item that isn't just a config default |
| **Convergence / noise mitigation** | (a) increase feedback iterations for these runs specifically, (b) run each site multiple times and average, (c) accept single-run noise and caveat results | Needs input from whoever maintains the TDM's feedback-loop scripts — no Control Center lever was found for this | Results could be dominated by run-to-run noise rather than the effect being measured |

## Effort and runtime

Each Test/Control scenario needs a **full feedback run** (mode choice
logsums + four-period assignment) — households are added before
disaggregation, so nothing upstream can be skipped or reused between sites.
Only the Base run benefits from reuse. Runtime scales linearly with number
of sites; `max_parallel_runs` (already supported, not yet exercised on a
real multi-scenario batch) could help once Cube Voyager licensing/hardware
limits on this workstation are confirmed.

Suggested build order:
1. Confirm the Base-run reuse strategy and the driver-script edit; validate
   `Summary_HighwayNet.csv` comes out as expected on the existing Base run alone.
2. Build SE generation + one real site + the Murray control; validate the
   ΔVHT / Burden Index math end-to-end on real output before committing to
   the full site list.
3. Once proven, add the remaining sites from the confirmed list.

## Bottom line

The metric, the SE-modification mechanism, and the run-set framework are all
already proven in this repo for other studies — this is a matter of
configuration and one small driver-script change, not new engineering. What's
missing before this can start is **the site list** and **a convergence
strategy**; both need a decision from outside this repo before any model time
is spent.
